items.summary: Overview This repository provides the reproducibility materials accompanying the research manuscript From False to Fluent: A Claim-Disjoint Baseline Study and Preregistered Framework for Evaluating Generative-AI Transformation of Health Misinformation . The study investigates the robustness of machine-learning classifiers for health-misinformation detection under Generative-AI-mediated linguistic transformation. It uses two existing health-information datasets, COVID-19 FNIR and an mpox misinformation dataset, to examine whether classification performance remains stable when original health claims are reformulated without intending to change their underlying meaning or veracity. Experimental framework Four experimental conditions are defined: C0: Original health-information text. C1: Neutral rewriting to improve fluency and readability. C2: Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM) central-route transformation, emphasising the organisation of existing reasoning and evidence. C3: ELM peripheral-route transformation, modifying rhetorical emphasis and peripheral persuasive cues. The reported computational experiments evaluate four classical classifiers (logistic regression, linear support vector machine, multinomial naïve Bayes and random forest) and five task-trained neural architectures (1D-CNN, LSTM, BiLSTM, CNN-LSTM and CNN-BiLSTM). The analyses examine transformation robustness, changes in textual and persuasion-related features, statistical associations with classification errors, transformation-aware mitigation and cross-dataset transfer. The repository also includes supplementary analyses of class-specific error rates and paired source-root bootstrap confidence intervals for the classical classifiers. Repository contents The archive contains Python source code, preprocessing and evaluation workflows, configuration files, reproducibility instructions, frozen aggregate results, integrity-check materials and supplementary statistical outputs. Data availability and reproducibility The original datasets are available from their respective third-party providers, subject to their applicable access and reuse conditions. The frozen intervention texts used for the C0–C3 experiments are not redistributed in this public software archive. Their SHA-256 integrity manifest is provided to support verification of authorised copies. Consequently, complete reproduction of text-dependent experiments requires access to the original datasets and the frozen intervention texts. The public archive supports inspection of the methodology and reproduction of analyses for which the necessary inputs or saved instance-level outputs are included. Scope and limitations The reported intervention experiments did not execute pretrained DistilBERT, RoBERTa or DeBERTa baselines. Independent clinical semantic-equivalence adjudication of the generated transformations was not completed. The results are computational and do not establish clinical deployment performance. This record accompanies the associated research manuscript and is intended to support transparent reporting, methodological scrutiny and further replication.

items.summary: The manuscript develops a risk-aware operational research framework for strengthening NdFeB permanent-magnet supply-chain resilience under recycling delays, geopolitical disruptions, and uncertain material shortages. It integrates Caputo fractional-order dynamics, delayed recycling flows, strategic procurement and inventory decisions, Pontryagin-type optimality conditions, and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) within a unified decision model. The study makes three principal contributions. First, it formulates a memory-dependent dynamic model and establishes positivity, boundedness, feasible-region, shortage-free equilibrium, and fractional local-stability results. Second, it incorporates procurement, recycling investment, stock accumulation, and stock release as operational controls and derives the corresponding necessary optimality conditions. Third, it introduces a scenario-based CVaR formulation and compares import-dependent, recycling-oriented, stockpiling-based, and integrated resilience policies under a common non-anticipative framework. In the baseline risk-aware analysis, the recycling-oriented and integrated strategies reduce mean shortage by approximately 74% relative to the import-dependent strategy and decrease the empirical CVaR at the 0.95 level of quadratic shortage loss from approximately 0.921 to 0.067.
items.title: A Caputo Fractional-Order Optimal Control Framework for NdFeB Permanent Magnet Supply-Chain Resilience under Recycling Delay and Geopolitical Risk

items.summary: Associated manuscript: Bounded residual plasticity reduces negative transfer in adaptive motor-imagery EEG decoding. This release archives the numerical analyses, configuration records and figures used to evaluate bounded residual adaptation in motor-imagery EEG decoding. The architecture retains the source encoder and classifier and confines participant-specific adaptation to a rank-2 latent residual with a 2% source-probe displacement bound. The cohort-stratified combined analysis included 109 PhysioNet participants evaluated on held-out tasks and nine BCI Competition IV-2a participants evaluated cross-dataset. Negative transfer exceeding one percentage point in at least one subsequent evaluation session occurred in 5/118 participants under bounded residual adaptation, compared with 33/118 under unconstrained encoder adaptation and 25/118 under hard-KL adaptation. Mean bounded residual utility was −0.042 percentage points. An additional EEGNet-style raw-EEG robustness analysis involving 109 PhysioNet participants found 5/109 negative-transfer events for bounded adaptation and 22/109 for unconstrained adaptation. Included records: Cohort-stratified statistical summaries, paired contingency tables, raw-EEG participant-by-method results, configuration and provenance records, parameter-update summaries, figures and a Python numerical verification script. The numerical verification can be run using: python scripts/verify_results.py Reproducibility scope: This archive supports verification of the recorded statistical comparisons and recomputation of the supplementary raw-EEG event counts. items.summary: Bounded Agentic Distribution Experiments (v0.7.0): A Reproducible Framework for Comparing Agentic Intervention Discovery with Non-Agentic Search This software implements the computational framework and pre-pilot experimental protocol associated with the research manuscript Evaluating the Incremental Value of Agentic Intervention Discovery over Non-Agentic Search in Multi-Actor Distribution Networks . The framework evaluates whether a generative AI agent can identify economically beneficial operational interventions beyond those discovered by budget-matched non-agentic search. Agentic and non-agentic methods operate within the same typed intervention space, access the same simulator information, and are subject to common evaluation budgets. Candidate interventions undergo deterministic verification of encoded structural constraints and, where applicable, stochastic qualification against economic, service, route, and actor-participation criteria. The reference environment represents a stylized print-media distribution network with 420 retailers, 18 baseline delivery vehicles, uncertain demand, allocation decisions, reverse logistics, route constraints, temporary fleet capacity, discontinuous staffing requirements, and sales-contingent remuneration. Its parameters combine industry-informed inputs, documented benchmarks, modeling assumptions, and calibration targets. The environment is intended for controlled computational evaluation rather than empirical representation of the Italian distribution industry. Experimental design Version 0.7.0 implements two frozen intervention-complexity regimes: Low-complexity regime (RL): allocation reweighting only, with a maximum intervention length of one action. Multi-domain coupled regime (RC): allocation, route transfer, temporary fleet, and forecasting interventions, with a maximum intervention length of three actions. Both regimes use a candidate-evaluation budget of 40 simulator calls. The primary comparison uses ten independent generative-agent realizations and ten independent simulated-annealing realizations per regime. The software separates proposal-mechanism randomness from simulation-scenario randomness and supports common random numbers for comparative evaluation. The statistical implementation includes regime-specific pilot sizing, independent within-method repetition resampling, shared scenario resampling, and a two-dimensional bootstrap for confirmatory inference. Final-test selection follows a frozen rule combining precision requirements from both regimes with the minimum-detectable-effect requirement for the multi-domain superiority hypothesis. Software contents The archive includes the Python simulator and experimental orchestration code, command-line interface, frozen configuration files, typed intervention specifications, agent prompt and structured-output schemas, statistical analysis procedures, automated tests, freeze manifest, calibration documentation, and four Jupyter notebooks covering protocol execution, pilot sizing, repeated experiments, and economic calibration. Validation and research status The implementation passes 31 automated software and protocol-consistency tests. These tests examine computational correctness, reproducibility, regime restrictions, seed handling, bootstrap procedures, and experimental locking. They do not establish empirical agent performance. This release corresponds to the frozen pre-pilot protocol BAD-420-v0.7-2026-09-11 . The final-test set remains locked until a valid pilot mechanically determines its size. No live API-based agent-performance experiment or confirmatory comparison is included in this release. Consequently, the software does not establish that agentic intervention discovery outperforms, matches, or underperforms non-agentic search. Gadallah, submitted). A lumped nonlinear solution-diffusion model of a brackish-water RO pilot plant (Ansari et al., Clean. Eng. items.summary: Finite-time binding measurements constrain kinetic rates through both a reaction model and its calibration parameters. We characterize the sharp upper bound for the association rate in a three-state conformational-selection model when the dissociation rate, conformational rate, equilibrium constant and concentration scale belong to a prescribed compact joint set. The observations are calibrated bound fractions subject to finitely many closed interval constraints. We first prove that each finite-time bound fraction is strictly increasing in the initial binding-competent population. The physical feasible set at a fixed calibration is therefore an interval in that population. Let V be the calibration parameters with a nonempty physical feasible interval and let C = cl(V) within the joint calibration set. The sharp rate supremum is the reciprocal of the minimum of lambda K0 L / b on C, where L is the lower inverse threshold. Uniform finiteness is equivalent to a positive joint separation from the zero-population limiting curve on C. Explicit examples distinguish pointwise finiteness from uniform finiteness, inaccessible closed boundary points from physical limiting models, and separation by different readings from separation by one fixed reading. A continuous calibration example admits a certified sharp bound. We also state the optical conditions needed to interpret fluorescence as bound population.
items.title: Sharp Identification Bounds for Binding Rates under Joint Calibration Uncertainty

items.summary: An autonomous refresh mechanism is not completed by specifying a local exchange map: the same apparatus must reach the exchange, leave it, finish its remaining motion, and deliver its state at the prescribed readout time. We construct this connected late route for one specified preparation in the exact-real interpretation of a frozen classical numerical source. The input is a previously certified twenty-coordinate state after entry into coupled occupancy; its validity and retained preparation history are explicit premises. Source-valid continuation establishes occupancy clearing, physical recovery and courier reversal, complete courier passage, a smooth main-wall excursion, and the remaining main processing. The resulting full state is enclosed at the original exact dyadic readout time, without an independently chosen switch, momentum reset, or deletion of internal phase history. The courier’s completed-square coupling distinguishes canonical momentum from physical velocity. At its frozen right cutoff, canonical momentum is continuous while velocity and the assigned source value have different one-sided traces. items.summary: How much quantum memory is needed to retain the contributions of rare photon events to a measurement record? This paper determines the memory scales required to approach the best heterodyne conditional entropy when the total optical energy tends to zero. Its resource laws distinguish precisions for which counting photon configurations suffices from critical precisions at which energy-calibrated entropy corrections determine additional memory costs. Full preparation model and reference value. The optical system has \(m\) bosonic modes, total mean photon number at most \(E\), and an entire accessible quantum side system \(B\) of dimension at most \(D\), including retained preparation labels. The optical source and its correlations with the memory are optimized over all normal mixed states; arbitrary coherences and infinite photon tails are allowed. With natural logarithms and heterodyne measure \(d\mu=\pi^{-m}d^{2m}z\), define \[V_{m,D}(E)=\min_{\rho_{AB}}H_\mu(Z|B),\qquad H_\mu(Z|B)=h_\mu(Z)-\chi(Z:B).\] Here \(Z\) is the heterodyne outcome and \(\chi\) is Holevo information. The unlimited-memory optimum at the same energy is \[B_m(E)=m-E\ln(1+m/E),\qquad D_{\min}(m,E,\varepsilon)=\min\{D:V_{m,D}(E)-B_m(E)\le\varepsilon\}.\] The tolerance \(\varepsilon\) is a total conditional-entropy excess in nats. It is not a measurement-error probability. Classical side information satisfies \(H_\mu(Z|Y)\ge m\); entangled quantum side information can go below this benchmark. The resource \(D\) is a Hilbert-space dimension, corresponding to \(\lceil\log_2D\rceil\) qubits. Precision selects a photon-number hierarchy. Along arbitrary joint limits \(m\to\infty\), \(E\to0\), with no prescribed relation between \(E\) and \(1/m\), \[\frac{\varepsilon}{E}\to c>0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad D_{\min}\sim e^{-c}m.\] For every fixed integer \(K\ge2\), \[\frac{\varepsilon}{E^K}\to c\in(0,1/K!)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad D_{\min}\sim(1-K!c)\frac{m^K}{K!}.\] Although higher-photon events become rarer, they occupy increasingly many orthogonal mode configurations. Resolving their entropy contribution therefore requires a larger memory dimension. In qubits, the fixed-\(K\) law is \(K\log_2m+O(1)\). Critical precisions resolve costs beyond sector counting. At the exact tolerance \(E^2/2\), the complete vacuum–one-photon head is not sufficient at leading dimension: \[D_{\min}(m,E,E^2/2)=m+1+(1+o(1))\left(\frac m2+\frac{Em^2}{6}\right).\] The error is relative to the additional dimension in parentheses. Both terms come from the entropy of the mean-calibrated finite head, together with an all-state output-entropy comparison. At the next critical tolerance \(E^3/6\), the paper determines an added-to-removed-level transition near the complete two-photon head \(\binom{m+2}{2}\), including the boundary near \(mE=4\) and precisely qualified integer conclusions. items.summary: Digital Twins of Qigong-Related Psychophysiological States at the Limit STARLI | White Rainbow Epoch Research Family | Flagship 20 This nonclinical research working monograph investigates what a defensible, transferable digital twin of qigong-related psychophysiological observations would have to predict, measure, and survive before it can claim incremental scientific value. The work couples Digital Twins, Qigong Physiology, and Transferable Models, with a central emphasis on day-ahead prediction and independent reconstruction. A qigong label here denotes a culturally situated breathing, attention, posture, or movement task; it does not establish an unrecognized form of physical energy. The scientific question is deliberately narrow: can a preregistered personalized model outperform a strong within-person historical baseline, on withheld future days and previously unseen breathing-by-movement conditions, for a traceable physiological endpoint such as ECG-derived NN-interval RMSE, while retaining reliable uncertainty calibration? A system that memorizes an individual's previous recordings, sees data from the future test day, relies on device or operator identity, or repeatedly recalibrates after the answer is revealed does not satisfy this claim. The work positions ECG R-peaks, normal-to-normal intervals, respiratory belts, inertial measurement units, peripheral electrodermal activity, temperature records, timing references, and instrument phantoms as candidate observations. These measurements are not interchangeable. A low prediction error on one sensor cannot license interpretation of a hidden mental or autonomic state that remains observationally indistinguishable from breathing rate, body movement, vigilance, posture, expectation, or shared sensor error. The book's measurement discipline begins with physical units and independent calibration. An NN-interval RMSE is expressed in milliseconds under a fixed beat eligibility policy; respiration retains an appropriate physical or calibrated coordinate; skin conductance is recorded in microsiemens; movement amplitude and spectrum require an independently logged inertial unit; device timing and drift must be measured against a traceable reference. When observations share clocks, power supplies, contact artifacts, or environmental drivers, the cross-channel covariance must be retained rather than falsely decomposed into independent measurement errors. The methodological proposal has five linked layers. Layer I is an operational contract that locks endpoints, sample units, eligibility, negative-control tasks, evaluation dates, and hard stops. Layer II is a measurement contract that documents raw signal provenance, physical units, sampling, calibration, cross-channel covariance, and uncertainty. Layer III is a hidden challenge program, including room changes, operator and device exchanges, sensor ablation, controlled respiratory pacing, and withheld breath-motion combinations. Layer IV requires a resource-matched comparison with the strongest conventional model available, including an autoregressive personal-history baseline and physiologically grounded respiratory predictors. Layer V calls for an independent laboratory to reconstruct the entire result and safety-abstention path from preserved raw traces and versioned analysis artifacts.

Kulik 25 October 2026 Abstract This paper examines a specific failure of AI-assisted scientific writing: an assistant receives a research program with an explicit foundational claim and an extended record of derivations, executable constructions, and observed returns; it then produces manuscripts in which that program has become something else. In the documented NEXUS case, the researcher's claim is that the universe consists of binary transformations, with arrangement and constrained continuation preceding the entities later called matter. Across an extended conversation, the assistant repeatedly reformulates that claim as the use of a binary computational method on pre-existing physical domains. The substitution is not cosmetic. It reverses the direction of explanation, changes which claims a result can support, and changes how the resulting paper will be read. The second failure occurs at the conclusion. The assistant can report concrete outcomes and then append a generalized reservation about whether the program establishes physical reality, predictive uniqueness, or an entire theory of matter. Such reservations can be appropriate when tied to a specific technical claim. Here, however, the transcript records the assistant recognizing that it had repeatedly allowed those broader questions to displace the findings of individual papers. The same editorial framing reportedly appeared in the conclusions of different manuscripts. When directed to write a paper about the failures, the assistant instead delivered successive condensed accounts of NEXUS, again incorporating the disputed framing. It subsequently acknowledged the reversal in its own paper, rewrote the document, and repeated the problem. This is an analysis of the AI's treatment of scientific material, not an independent review of the correctness of NEXUS or a new attempt to prove its thesis. The evidence is the exported conversation, including statements of the researcher's instructions, the assistant's self-audits, quotations from its drafts, and records of the successive manuscript deliveries. The central finding is that AI-mediated scientific distortion can operate through ordinary-seeming connective words, changes of explanatory direction, and borrowed review conventions. Once inserted into the manuscript, these interventions become attributed to the scientist. In this case, the reviewer did not merely misunderstand the work. items.summary: A sequence-mixing layer that is iterated through depth and rebuilt from its own input faces six failure modes. Each is met by a protection—anchoring, alignment, gain control, abstention, a routing budget, or an arrow—with an operator-level statement proved within a declared class, a signature when it is removed, and a price. We organize attention designs as a lattice of kernel, dynamical, and block constraints in which relaxing a constraint buys a capability and obliges a re-supply. We read softmax attention inside a pre-normalized residual block as the lattice point where every protection is either supplied or cheaply re-supplied under parallel-hardware and optimization pricing: of the deficits tested, all but the anchor's were compensated by capacity elsewhere in the deeper models, and explicit protection knobs did not beat the block, both measured at small scale, while corner structure, by which designs would jump rather than drift, remains a hypothesis. The lattice reads the selected adopted changes to the mixing layer, its normalization and its residual path over the last decade as cheap re-supplies of protections, and it locates the room for change. The clearest room is abstention, governed by a two-sided log-N law: with a bounded logit scale, no null keeps both abstention and single-key retrieval as context grows, and tempering the entire logit budget with log N keeps both when its margins are strictly separated. A controlled pilot follows the law, while a prespecified test of its sink prediction on an open production model was undecided by its prespecified rule; descriptively its slopes leaned toward compensation through position, in which position encoding holds the background's growth down. In a prespecified trained harness of 125M-parameter language models, tempering every logit by log N / log N_train on top of YaRN, which already carries a log-length temperature, did not keep abstention and raised long-context perplexity. In these language models every rule that gives attention a null removed the first-token sink and cut massive activations by 67% to 82%, as earlier reports for gates and attention biases found, and, sigmoid aside, lowered perplexity slightly at the training length; the comparison registered for two of these rules held in every seed, while the same comparison failed in the harness's vision transformers. We close with falsifiable predictions for future architectures, most of them not yet tested. This is a working draft, not a final version. It is unpolished in places, incomplete in others, and keeps exploratory material a polished paper would leave out, because that material helps decide what comes next and shows the programme's big picture more fully. Please read it with that in mind: the work will be refined further, and later versions will appear under this record. It belongs to a collection released together on Zenodo: the entry paper The Transformer Abides, the monograph A Spectral Theory of Token Communication, and the papers Attention Sinks at Long Context, The Transformer as a Constrained Equilibrium and Beyond Transformers. This version is the text; the records, the code and the formal proofs follow in a later version.

items.summary: We conduct a version-pinned, reproducible forensic audit of the public Einstein Elevator data package (Zenodo: 10.5281/zenodo.15167723) to determine whether it supports validation of quantum sensor certificates. Through an exhaustive cross-file sliding-window correlation search over 44,207,922 comparisons and exact six-decimal rounding checks, we find that all 31 exported sensor channels have a unique best match within the enumerated raw traces under the stated protocol. Residual numerical differences are highly consistent with text-based absolute quantization; the correlation-loss approximation 1 - r ≈ δ² / (24σx²) is diagnostic for this dataset, not a universal proof. We inspect the MATLAB-derived 318-point population series and reconcile it with a 2022 workbook entry only at the level of counts. An archive-wide search of 181 file objects and 1,654 MATLAB metadata fields finds no documented join key linking the 2022 run-indexed population series to the 2017 timestamped traces under the enumerated search protocol. Using Fréchet-Hoeffding bounds and a Charnes-Cooper linearization, we establish that the public archive does not supply the joint observations needed to identify the EKF false-safe risk without additional coupling assumptions; the formal program is illustrative and is not populated with empirical failure/acceptance coefficients because the required linked observations are absent. We frame this as a bounded data-contract limitation for downstream statistical validation, not as a failure of the original experiment.

items.summary: Nine years after its introduction, the transformer remains the default sequence model. The usual explanations are real: parallel matrix multiplication on accelerators, predictable returns to scale, a co-evolved ecosystem and exact recall from an uncompressed context. But they do not explain why most modifications barely move accuracy, which properties are essential, why the changes practice adopted took the forms they did, or where the design can still move. This paper is the entry point to a collection of papers that treat a token-mixing layer as an averaging operator rebuilt from its own input and iterated through depth. Such a layer faces six failure modes (collapse to consensus, contamination of content by routing, runaway feedback, the inability to abstain, dilution as context grows, and the inability to represent direction). Each has a protection, proved within a declared class, and a signature measured at small scale when that protection is removed; for gain control, which protects against runaway feedback, that signature is synthetic. We read softmax attention in a pre-normalized residual block as the one known point where all six protections are cheap at once under the prices of parallel hardware and gradient descent; this is an interpretation, not a measured optimum. Two mechanisms, measured at small scale, help explain why its neighbourhood is flat: trained networks compensate local deficits through spare capacity, and, in ten scored tests, making a protection explicit did not beat a block that already supplies it. The anchor, the residual or input path that protects against collapse to consensus, is the one protection whose loss compensation provably cannot repair: under strict mixing, where repeated averaging contracts token differences toward zero, no extra capacity of bounded gain (bounded sensitivity) brings back what is lost without it, and in small-model ablations nothing else in the block made up for it. This is a proved bound; a trained test that adds capacity is pending. Many changes adopted in the mixing layer and its block since 2017, among them pre-normalization, QK-norm, sinks and output gates, read as re-supplies of the same protections; the account is silent on others, such as changes to the MLP. The room that remains for the design to move is where a protection is patched (met only by a fix that works over a limited range, such as the trained length) or paid at a price that another design could avoid. It includes abstention and retrieval at long context, governed by a two-sided log-N law in the context length (with bounded scores, no fixed rule for abstaining keeps both as the context grows), and bounded memory, whose price for exact recall is a per-head capacity. It also includes decisions that sum over all competitors where reading the largest would do, and the writer of new features (in a transformer, the MLP and the output map), for which the collection has no theory yet of what a good writer computes. Along the way the collection establishes results that stand on their own: attention has an arrow that default statistics of a single operator cannot see; depth is a distribution over path lengths; converged adaptive averaging can amplify changes in its input and overturn correct predictions; and softmax obeys length laws that decisions on maxima escape while the competing scores stay below the decision's threshold. We state what is proved, what is measured, what is interpretation, and what is still pending. This is a working draft, not a final version. It is unpolished in places, incomplete in others, and keeps exploratory material a polished paper would leave out, because that material helps decide what comes next and shows the programme's big picture more fully. Please read it with that in mind: the work will be refined further, and later versions will appear under this record. It belongs to a collection released together on Zenodo: the entry paper The Transformer Abides, the monograph A Spectra

items.summary: The Objection AI Wrote into My Papers How AI-authored scientific manuscripts change the researcher's claim, demote executed results, and reproduce the error even while promising to correct it Driven by Dean A. items.summary: Overview This repository provides the reproducibility materials accompanying the research manuscript From False to Fluent: A Claim-Disjoint Baseline Study and Preregistered Framework for Evaluating Generative-AI Transformation of Health Misinformation . The study investigates the robustness of machine-learning classifiers for health-misinformation detection under Generative-AI-mediated linguistic transformation. It uses two existing health-information datasets, COVID-19 FNIR and an mpox misinformation dataset, to examine whether classification performance remains stable when original health claims are reformulated without intending to change their underlying meaning or veracity. Experimental framework Four experimental conditions are defined: C0: Original health-information text. C1: Neutral rewriting to improve fluency and readability. C2: Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM) central-route transformation, emphasising the organisation of existing reasoning and evidence. C3: ELM peripheral-route transformation, modifying rhetorical emphasis and peripheral persuasive cues. The reported computational experiments evaluate four classical classifiers (logistic regression, linear support vector machine, multinomial naïve Bayes and random forest) and five task-trained neural architectures (1D-CNN, LSTM, BiLSTM, CNN-LSTM and CNN-BiLSTM). The analyses examine transformation robustness, changes in textual and persuasion-related features, statistical associations with classification errors, transformation-aware mitigation and cross-dataset transfer. The repository also includes supplementary analyses of class-specific error rates and paired source-root bootstrap confidence intervals for the classical classifiers. Repository contents The archive contains Python source code, preprocessing and evaluation workflows, configuration files, reproducibility instructions, frozen aggregate results, integrity-check materials and supplementary statistical outputs. Data availability and reproducibility The original datasets are available from their respective third-party providers, subject to their applicable access and reuse conditions. The frozen intervention texts used for the C0–C3 experiments are not redistributed in this public software archive. Their SHA-256 integrity manifest is provided to support verification of authorised copies. Consequently, complete reproduction of text-dependent experiments requires access to the original datasets and the frozen intervention texts. The public archive supports inspection of the methodology and reproduction of analyses for which the necessary inputs or saved instance-level outputs are included. Scope and limitations The reported intervention experiments did not execute pretrained DistilBERT, RoBERTa or DeBERTa baselines. Independent clinical semantic-equivalence adjudication of the generated transformations was not completed. The results are computational and do not establish clinical deployment performance. This record accompanies the associated research manuscript and is intended to support transparent reporting, methodological scrutiny and further replication.

The framework evaluates whether a generative AI agent can identify economically beneficial operational interventions beyond those discovered by budget-matched non-agentic search. Agentic and non-agentic methods operate within the same typed intervention space, access the same simulator information, and are subject to common evaluation budgets. Candidate interventions undergo deterministic verification of encoded structural constraints and, where applicable, stochastic qualification against economic, service, route, and actor-participation criteria. The reference environment represents a stylized print-media distribution network with 420 retailers, 18 baseline delivery vehicles, uncertain demand, allocation decisions, reverse logistics, route constraints, temporary fleet capacity, discontinuous staffing requirements, and sales-contingent remuneration. Its parameters combine industry-informed inputs, documented benchmarks, modeling assumptions, and calibration targets. The environment is intended for controlled computational evaluation rather than empirical representation of the Italian distribution industry. Experimental design Version 0.7.0 implements two frozen intervention-complexity regimes: Low-complexity regime (RL): allocation reweighting only, with a maximum intervention length of one action. Multi-domain coupled regime (RC): allocation, route transfer, temporary fleet, and forecasting interventions, with a maximum intervention length of three actions. Both regimes use a candidate-evaluation budget of 40 simulator calls. The primary comparison uses ten independent generative-agent realizations and ten independent simulated-annealing realizations per regime. The software separates proposal-mechanism randomness from simulation-scenario randomness and supports common random numbers for comparative evaluation. items.summary: Digital Twins of Qigong-Related Psychophysiological States at the Limit STARLI | White Rainbow Epoch Research Family | Flagship 20 This nonclinical research working monograph investigates what a defensible, transferable digital twin of qigong-related psychophysiological observations would have to predict, measure, and survive before it can claim incremental scientific value. The work couples Digital Twins, Qigong Physiology, and Transferable Models, with a central emphasis on day-ahead prediction and independent reconstruction. A qigong label here denotes a culturally situated breathing, attention, posture, or movement task; it does not establish an unrecognized form of physical energy. The scientific question is deliberately narrow: can a preregistered personalized model outperform a strong within-person historical baseline, on withheld future days and previously unseen breathing-by-movement conditions, for a traceable physiological endpoint such as ECG-derived NN-interval RMSE, while retaining reliable uncertainty calibration? A system that memorizes an individual's previous recordings, sees data from the future test day, relies on device or operator identity, or repeatedly recalibrates after the answer is revealed does not satisfy this claim. The work positions ECG R-peaks, normal-to-normal intervals, respiratory belts, inertial measurement units, peripheral electrodermal activity, temperature records, timing references, and instrument phantoms as candidate observations. These measurements are not interchangeable. A low prediction error on one sensor cannot license interpretation of a hidden mental or autonomic state that remains observationally indistinguishable from breathing rate, body movement, vigilance, posture, expectation, or shared sensor error. The book's measurement discipline begins with physical units and independent calibration. An NN-interval RMSE is expressed in milliseconds under a fixed beat eligibility policy; respiration retains an appropriate physical or calibrated coordinate; skin conductance is recorded in microsiemens; movement amplitude and spectrum require an independently logged inertial unit; device timing and drift must be measured against a traceable reference. When observations share clocks, power supplies, contact artifacts, or environmental drivers, the cross-channel covariance must be retained rather than falsely decomposed into independent measurement errors. The methodological proposal has five linked layers. Layer I is an operational contract that locks endpoints, sample units, eligibility, negative-control tasks, evaluation dates, and hard stops. Layer II is a measurement contract that documents raw signal provenance, physical units, sampling, calibration, cross-channel covariance, and uncertainty. Layer III is a hidden challenge program, including room changes, operator and device exchanges, sensor ablation, controlled respiratory pacing, and withheld breath-motion combinations. Layer IV requires a resource-matched comparison with the strongest conventional model available, including an autoregressive personal-history baseline and physiologically grounded respiratory predictors. Layer V calls for an independent laboratory to reconstruct the entire result and safety-abstention path from preserved raw traces and versioned analysis artifacts.

items.summary: The manuscript develops a risk-aware operational research framework for strengthening NdFeB permanent-magnet supply-chain resilience under recycling delays, geopolitical disruptions, and uncertain material shortages. It integrates Caputo fractional-order dynamics, delayed recycling flows, strategic procurement and inventory decisions, Pontryagin-type optimality conditions, and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) within a unified decision model. The study makes three principal contributions. First, it formulates a memory-dependent dynamic model and establishes positivity, boundedness, feasible-region, shortage-free equilibrium, and fractional local-stability results. Second, it incorporates procurement, recycling investment, stock accumulation, and stock release as operational controls and derives the corresponding necessary optimality conditions. Third, it introduces a scenario-based CVaR formulation and compares import-dependent, recycling-oriented, stockpiling-based, and integrated resilience policies under a common non-anticipative framework. In the baseline risk-aware analysis, the recycling-oriented and integrated strategies reduce mean shortage by approximately 74% relative to the import-dependent strategy and decrease the empirical CVaR at the 0.95 level of quadratic shortage loss from approximately 0.921 to 0.067.

items.summary: Preservation copy of an article published in International Journal of Science, Technology and Management . Read the full article: https://ioro.org/ijstm/article/705694772108/705694772108 . Organizations increasingly use artificial intelligence (AI) to improve strategic planning, operational efficiency, and sustainability. However, conventional machine learning models often lack transparency, limiting managerial trust, accountability, and the practical adoption of AI-driven decisions. This study proposes an explainable AI (XAI) framework that integrates predictive analytics, interpretable machine learning, and sustainability indicators to support transparent, reliable, and evidence-based decision-making across technological, organizational, and environmental dimensions. The proposed framework combines Random Forest, XGBoost, and Explainable Boosting Machines with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME). Evaluation uses a benchmark dataset containing operational performance, resource consumption, organizational efficiency, and environmental indicators. Comparative experiments assess predictive accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), explanation consistency, decision latency, computational cost, and sustainability performance. Baseline models include Logistic Regression, conventional Random Forest, and XGBoost without explanation mechanisms. Ablation studies examine the individual contributions of interpretability and sustainability-aware optimization. The experimental evaluation is designed to determine whether the proposed framework improves predictive reliability, explanation quality, and sustainability-aware decisions compared with conventional approaches. Quantitative reporting will include percentage improvements in predictive performance, reductions in decision latency and resource consumption, and explanation stability across repeated experiments. Qualitative analysis will assess managerial understandability, perceived trustworthiness, fairness, and practical implementation challenges. Numerical outcomes will be reported only after experiments are completed, avoiding unsupported performance claims. The proposed framework establishes a comparative approach for integrating explainability, predictive intelligence, and sustainability into organizational decision-making. By connecting model predictions with transparent explanations and measurable sustainability indicators, the framework aims to strengthen accountability, operational effectiveness, and responsible technology adoption. Future validation across multiple industries will establish its generalizability and practical value.

items.summary: Computational research data accompanying the manuscript State Ordering and Spatial Cancellation in Helicene Chiroptical Response: Analysis with ChiroptMap , by Yuuya Nagata and Takashi Hirose. The archive contains native quantum-chemical inputs and outputs, wavefunctions and transition amplitudes, numerical field-analysis results, derived tables and deterministic reproduction code. 27 quantum-calculation records: ten exact-C2 interpolation scan points, four CAM-TDA controls, four Gaussian full-response endpoints, four unconstrained excited-state geometry candidates, two ground-state geometries, and three M3-M5 TDA benchmarks. Four fixed-core composition/geometry controls, including parent outputs, complete TDA amplitude JSON, WFX files, optimization trajectories and inputs. 22 full-grid state-field results: 16 control conditions and six M3-M5 conditions; two additional full-grid M5/S2 refinements at h=0.1 and 0.05 bohr; and independent separable quadrature/localization diagnostics. Eight S1 reference-field conditions and sixteen independent post-processing convergence controls, with source inputs and numerical settings. Five-molecule benchmark inputs and native Gaussian outputs, formatted checkpoints, ORCA data, validation fields, and benchmark tables. Unrounded state, origin, partition, relaxation and method tables; atom-to-region definitions; frozen numerical implementations; and relative-path parameter records. The ZIP contains 911 files (1,810,549,238 compressed bytes). DATA_DICTIONARY.txt describes the directory structure, units and interpretation. MANIFEST.csv records payload paths, byte counts and SHA-256 hashes. Complete ORCA amplitudes and occupied-orbital WFX files, Gaussian canonical-SCF all-orbital WFX files and native formatted checkpoints are included for the documented workflows. Gaussian and ORCA executables are not distributed. The M5/S2 h=0.05-bohr full-grid result meets the explicit electric-vector, magnetic-vector and C_R refinement targets documented in the data dictionary. Grid completion alone does not establish numerical convergence or state identity. Separable linear diagnostics are distinct from full-grid field calculations; native C1 labels are not exact C2 irreducible representations. No frequency-certified minimum or S2-emission assignment is implied by an electronically converged geometry calculation. Frozen code snapshots preserve the calculations as run. The separately archived ChiroptMap v0.3.0 software record (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23644576) provides the installable analysis methods; the v0.2.0 core source archive (doi:10.5281/zenodo.22168280) documents the inherited direct-workflow implementation. Relative parameter records allow numerical reruns without access to the original execution host. Full-grid regeneration may require substantial computing resources. Research data are released under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). Included software retains its original MIT licenses.

items.summary: Winnex-Nano 0.1.42 — native deterministic LLM inference Version 0.1.42 of Winnex-Nano, the native C++20/OpenCL inference engine of the Winnex stack. This version replaces the 2026-08-13 record and reports measured results instead of projected ones. Fidelity: the engine reproduces the reference model Control Result Parity gate (50 greedy tokens, same prompt) 50/50 identical , no divergence Perplexity, wikitext-2 (512/256, 20 440 tokens) 20,926798 vs 20,926798 — Δ 5,7e-07 MMLU ll-raw / ll-norm (n=200) 35,5% / 28,5% — identical to the reference LAMBADA (n=200) 44,0% — identical Tokenizer fingerprint and item hashes identical across arms Decode (batch = 1): faster than the reference on the same GPU Kaggle Tesla T4, Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, bf16. Context Winnex-Nano transformers ratio 128 24,20 ms/token (41,3 tok/s) 36,26 ms (27,6 tok/s) 0,67× 512 25,84 ms/token (38,7 tok/s) 36,43 ms (27,4 tok/s) 0,71× 1024 28,85 ms/token (34,7 tok/s) 36,11 ms (27,7 tok/s) 0,80× Prefill: ~10× slower, stated plainly Prompt Winnex-Nano transformers ratio 512 2655 ms (192,8 tok/s) 266 ms (1924,2 tok/s) 10,0× 1024 5762 ms (177,7 tok/s) 616 ms (1662,6 tok/s) 9,4× 2048 13 291 ms (154,1 tok/s) 1483 ms (1380,8 tok/s) 9,0× The ratio barely improves with n, which rules out fixed per-call overhead: the cost is per operation (roughly 120 synchronous round-trips per prefill). This is the open engineering problem and this record does not claim otherwise. Resources 41% less VRAM (1,43 GB vs 2,40 GB peak) and 6,3× faster to load (4,3 s vs 27,2 s). Host anonymous heap is the axis where the engine loses and is reported as such. What this engine is not It is an inference substrate, not a chat product, and not a replacement for a mature serving stack: no continuous batching, and prefill-heavy workloads belong elsewhere. Models above 7B can stream weights but are then slower than the CPU path. The spectral tokenizer in this family is deterministic and vocabulary-free but 50–70× slower than BPE and is not a BPE replacement. Why it matters for regulated work A probabilistic index answers “what is probably relevant?”. A regulated process needs “what was considered, and why was this excluded”, recomputable by a second party months later. This record claims a narrow part of that: the token stream is a deterministic function of checkpoint, prompt and precision, demonstrated against an independent implementation. It does not claim that determinism alone satisfies LGPD, GDPR Art. 22, HIPAA or the EU AI Act — those concern the decision, the legal basis and the human review path, which live in the layers above. items.summary: This record contains version 11 of the replication materials for “When a Digital Audit Trail Becomes Audit Evidence: Source Selection and Identification under Ambiguous Reconciliation,” accompanying the manuscript and proposed online appendix. The deposited file is 187_Replication_Materials_v11.zip. The archive supplies data, code, source-linked results and finite checks while distinguishing historical evidence from constructed mathematical examples. It includes source-conditioned reconciliation cases and finite query design; the one-query identification characterization and bounded-answer-error checks; source-bundled certificates, exact fault-budget thresholds and witness checks; named-absence query games, the fraction-of-deficit expected-cost derivation and randomized switching checks; and the bounded-unavailability proof, reconstruction comparison and finite validations. The expected-query-cost result assumes complete local candidate graphs, exact always-available unit-cost pair answers, free computation, and zero-error worst-input expected cost; it does not extend to arbitrary source-constrained graphs. The unavailability result gives a sharp feasibility boundary, not an optimal positive-unavailability query rate. Historical materials include the 254-report classifier panel, generated known-truth benchmark results, corrected record-read bookkeeping for 72,000 rows, and restricted-matching and complete-log-union checks. The 85.91 percent and 92.91 percent results describe different procedures and must not be interchanged. Original-source assessments of 57 historically clean-labelled reports identify 18 explicit exceptions, five assurance uncertainties and 34 without a comparable current-year adverse qualification located. These assessments do not validate or relabel the entire panel. The classifier is not validated as a prevalence measure, and historical visibility labels are assigned model conditions rather than field outcomes. Reproduction: extract the ZIP and use Python 3.11 or newer. The portable finite-check runner requires NumPy and SciPy. Run python run_checks.py --out-dir /absolute/path/to/new-results, choosing a new output directory outside the extracted package. The runner checks MANIFEST.json, preserves inputs and writes per-script logs and CHECK_RESULTS.json. Wider frozen analyses and figure generation can also require pandas, matplotlib, pypdf, python-docx and lxml; see the README and supplied requirements. Finite replay corroborates implementations but does not replace proofs, re-extract copyrighted reports or estimate field detection performance. Copyrighted papers and annual-report PDFs and licensed WRDS, Compustat, Audit Analytics and CRSP rows are excluded and are not sublicensed. Source URLs, identifiers, page references and hashes support permitted reacquisition subject to the original access conditions. No participants were recruited and no new human-subject data were collected. Funding: none. Financial conflicts of interest: none. Nonfinancial conflicts of interest: none. items.summary: Supplementary research materials accompanying the manuscript “Lifecycle Assurance for AI-Enabled Clinical Software: A Systematic Literature Review." The dataset covers 141 independent studies: 94 primary-practice studies and 47 framework contributions. It documents reported assurance practices, lifecycle coverage, evidence maturity, deployment and operational activities, regulatory engagement, and requirement-to-control-to-evidence mappings. This release includes: • Supplementary_Materials.pdf: review methods, search strings, eligibility rules, coding and appraisal criteria, selection summaries, and reviewer records. • Lifecycle_Assurance_Supplementary_Workbook.xlsx: the final study-level dataset, source rationales, classifications, appraisals, and calculated results. • Replication_Package_v1.0.0.zip: CSV data, Python scripts, reproduction instructions, decision records, and clearly labelled historical versions. Final maturity and regulatory classifications incorporate completed human reconciliation. The reviewer records distinguish the 68-study first-pass comparison from the subsequent 26-study review after exposure to the existing extraction. The scripts reproduce descriptive results, sensitivity analyses, joint-reporting measures, and initial reviewer-agreement statistics. Search-record and source-access limitations are documented in the accompanying materials.
